item.title: Comment on Democracy, Capitalism and Monarchy (Yarvin) by nigel
item.description:
“The big question is not how Apple produces but how Apple is produced.”

Perfectly put. This is the key flaw in Yarvin’s thinking. It’s an amateurish mistake, since this is the central
problem of the political thinking that produced the American experiment.

Apple is the ultimate case of survivorship bias. The problem is making it work when you only get one roll of the dice, rather than picking one winner out of a sea of competitors, and the product is not laptops but civilization, and the means of production is the monopoly on violence and not factories and workers.

item.title: Comment on The Stargate Project by DanW
item.description:
And Elon tweets: "They don't actually have the money."

These tech announcements are so reminiscent of the dotcom bubble. There is the notion of unlimited money chasing big ideas, but no one knows how to actually make money on these ideas. So the same idea everyone knows - data centers - just gets blown up bigger and bigger.

All the while the hope is to spend other people's money because no one actually knows if these big ideas are profitable.
